title: BBC Chillers
paragraphs: A small BBC Radio 4 collection of full-cast horror and science-fiction dramatizations, built around unsettling stories and literary adaptations rather than a continuing cast or storyline.
Four-part BBC Radio 4 science-fiction/horror anthology adapted by Mike Walker from published stories.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: BBC Radio 4 Chillers (January 24, 2002 to February 14, 2002) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Mike Walker (radio adaptor), Ned Chaillet (director), Rachel Horan (director), Abi Eniola (performer), Ben Onwukwe (performer), Bill Bailey (performer), and Christopher Godwin (performer).

The stories often return to science fiction and speculative horror, literary radio adaptation, isolation and confinement, artificial intelligence and machine domination, Vietnam War and combat trauma, and telepathy and psychic connection.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes BBC Radio 4 Chillers four-part run and Modern BBC adaptation of classic and contemporary speculative fiction.
plain_text:
A small BBC Radio 4 collection of full-cast horror and science-fiction dramatizations, built around unsettling stories and literary adaptations rather than a continuing cast or storyline.

Four-part BBC Radio 4 science-fiction/horror anthology adapted by Mike Walker from published stories.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: BBC Radio 4 Chillers (January 24, 2002 to February 14, 2002) on BBC Radio 4.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Mike Walker (radio adaptor), Ned Chaillet (director), Rachel Horan (director), Abi Eniola (performer), Ben Onwukwe (performer), Bill Bailey (performer), and Christopher Godwin (performer).

The stories often return to science fiction and speculative horror, literary radio adaptation, isolation and confinement, artificial intelligence and machine domination, Vietnam War and combat trauma, and telepathy and psychic connection.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes BBC Radio 4 Chillers four-part run and Modern BBC adaptation of classic and contemporary speculative fiction.
